description: List the site/insurance-status groups with the largest share of conservation records. Return all rows whose share reaches the 10th-highest value, including every row tied at the cutoff.

b.request: For conservation records matched to sites by `scanconservation.zoneref = sites.zoneregistry`, group by site reference and insurance status, treating missing insurance status as its own group; return each group’s record count and its count divided by all matched conservation records, unrounded, including all groups tied at the 10th-highest share, sorted by share descending with missing statuses last
b.sql:
WITH group_counts AS (
  SELECT
    sc.zoneref,
    s.insurstat,
    COUNT(*) AS record_count
  FROM scanconservation AS sc
  JOIN sites AS s
    ON sc.zoneref = s.zoneregistry
  GROUP BY sc.zoneref, s.insurstat
),
shares AS (
  SELECT
    zoneref,
    insurstat,
    record_count,
    record_count::numeric / SUM(record_count) OVER () AS share
  FROM group_counts
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT
    zoneref,
    insurstat,
    record_count,
    share,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY share DESC) AS share_rank
  FROM shares
)
SELECT zoneref, insurstat, record_count, share
FROM ranked
WHERE share_rank <= 10
ORDER BY share DESC, insurstat NULLS LAST;

a.request: Match each conservation record (`scanconservation`) to its site where `sites.zoneregistry` equals `scanconservation.zoneref`, and drop records with no matching site. For each combination of site reference (`zoneref`) and insurance status (`insurstat`), with a missing status kept as its own value, show the site reference, the insurance status, the number of conservation records, and that number as a fraction of all matched conservation records, unrounded. Sort by that fraction from highest to lowest (missing last) and return every row whose fraction is at least the 10th-highest, keeping all rows tied at 10th place.
a.sql:
WITH grouped AS (
  SELECT sc.zoneref, s.insurstat, COUNT(*) AS conservation_record_count
  FROM scanconservation AS sc
  JOIN sites AS s ON s.zoneregistry = sc.zoneref
  GROUP BY sc.zoneref, s.insurstat
), ranked AS (
  SELECT zoneref, insurstat, conservation_record_count,
         conservation_record_count::numeric / SUM(conservation_record_count) OVER () AS fraction_of_matched_records,
         RANK() OVER (ORDER BY conservation_record_count::numeric / SUM(conservation_record_count) OVER () DESC NULLS LAST) AS fraction_rank
  FROM grouped
)
SELECT zoneref, insurstat, conservation_record_count, fraction_of_matched_records
FROM ranked
WHERE fraction_rank <= 10
ORDER BY fraction_of_matched_records DESC NULLS LAST;

c.request: Matching conservation records (`scanconservation`) to their sites on `zoneref` = `sites.zoneregistry` and dropping any without a site, which are the top 10 site reference and insurance status (`insurstat`) combinations by share of conservation records? Treat a missing status as its own value. Show the site reference, the insurance status, the record count, and the count as a fraction of all matched conservation records (unrounded), sorted by that fraction from highest to lowest with missing values last. List the site/insurance-status groups with the largest share of conservation records. Return all rows whose share reaches the 10th-highest value, including every row tied at the cutoff.
c.sql:
WITH matched AS (
  SELECT sc.zoneref, s.insurstat
  FROM scanconservation AS sc
  INNER JOIN sites AS s
    ON sc.zoneref = s.zoneregistry
), group_counts AS (
  SELECT zoneref, insurstat, COUNT(*) AS record_count,
         COUNT(*)::numeric / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS share
  FROM matched
  GROUP BY zoneref, insurstat
), ranked AS (
  SELECT *, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY share DESC) AS share_rank
  FROM group_counts
)
SELECT zoneref AS site_reference, insurstat AS insurance_status,
       record_count, share
FROM ranked
WHERE share_rank <= 10
ORDER BY share DESC, (insurstat IS NULL), zoneref;

d.request: For conservation records in `scanconservation` matched to sites where `zoneref = sites.zoneregistry`, excluding records without a matching site, list the site reference and insurance-status (`insurstat`) groups with the largest share of all matched records. Treat missing insurance status as its own value. Include each group’s record count and its unrounded fraction of all matched conservation records. Return all groups whose share is at least the 10th-highest share, including ties at the cutoff, and sort by share from highest to lowest with missing values last.
d.sql:
WITH group_counts AS (
  SELECT
    sc.zoneref,
    s.insurstat,
    COUNT(*) AS record_count
  FROM scanconservation AS sc
  INNER JOIN sites AS s
    ON sc.zoneref = s.zoneregistry
  GROUP BY sc.zoneref, s.insurstat
),
shares AS (
  SELECT
    zoneref,
    insurstat,
    record_count,
    record_count::numeric / SUM(record_count) OVER () AS share
  FROM group_counts
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT
    zoneref,
    insurstat,
    record_count,
    share,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY share DESC) AS share_rank
  FROM shares
)
SELECT zoneref, insurstat, record_count, share
FROM ranked
WHERE share_rank <= 10
ORDER BY share DESC, insurstat NULLS LAST, zoneref;
